          title: Email address

        postcode:
          title: Postcode

            within that region's range (NSW 2000-2099, VIC 3000-3099, QLD 4000-4099). A city

            household (same last name and postcode) with an existing owner. The
            householdId is computed regardless; this flag only bypasses the household
            duplicate block, so a matching owner is created as a declared household

The membership level was computed inline in `OwnerMapper` and hard-capped at 3 (`Math.min(3, ...)`), so level 4 was unreachable.

1. **New `MembershipLevels.of(owner)` helper** (`rest/function/common/MembershipLevels.java`) — keeps the existing pre-tenure factors (base 1, +1 for an email, +1 for `namesakeCount == 0`) capped at 3, then adds 1 for tenure. Tenure counts as qualifying only when `ChronoUnit.DAYS.between(registrationDate, today) > 365`. So the max a new owner (zero tenure) can reach is 3, and level 4 is reserved strictly for owners registered more than 365 days ago.

2. **`OwnerMapper`** — the `membershipLevel` mapping now delegates to `MembershipLevels.of(owner)`.

3. **`openapi.yml`** — raised the documented `maximum` from 3 to 4 and updated the description to spell out the tenure rule.

The `namesakeCount == 0` and email factors are the "pre-tenure" contributors that top out at 3; household size was never a formula factor (confirmed by Cp23, where a 3-member household member with no email stays at level 2), so the spec's "3-member household" phrasing is just illustrating a maxed-out new owner — still level 3, not 4. The new `Cp39Tests` (new owner capped at level 3) passes, and the existing level tests (Cp15, Cp23, Cp24) remain green.
